newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Australian opposition backs Malaysia crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Australian opposition backs Malaysia crackdown.

text.p: Australian opposition leader Kim Beazley on Monday backed Malaysia's crackdown on a conference on East Timor which resulted in the deportation of 46 foreigners, including an Australian bishop.

"Keeping people out of the country whose views we have problems with is not a process unknown in Australia," Labor party leader Beazley said when addressing members of the Australian business community in Jakarta.
"(British historian) David Irving and (Sinn Fein leader) Gerry Adams can testify to that," he said.
Both men were last week denied permission to enter Australia because the government said they failed to meet good character requirements of the Migration Act.
It said Adams is associated with the Provisional Irish Republican Army and Irving has consistently argued Hitler did not order the extermination of Jews during World War Two.
"It is entirely reasonable that a nation might determine what might be said by other people on its soil," Beazley said.

However, when answering questions about the impact of Australia's controversial racism debate and East Timor, Beazley said Australians were free to express views within their own country, including those critical of Jakarta's policies.
"We have a robust open democracy in Australia, so views are going to be expressed from time to time in Australia that people may take offence at," Beazley said.
"But it is the views of the Australian government that counts," he said.
Australian Prime Minister John Howard on Monday reacted to Malaysia's crackdown by telling Australians they had to live and let live.
"Let me simply say that different countries do things differently," he told reporters. "We do things our way, other countries do things their way."

Beazley also made an appeal to the Malaysian government not to punish Singapore-based Australian Broadcasting Corporation correspondent Catherine McGrath, who was one of those detained by authorities after the conference was disrupted.
"She was only doing her job," Beazley said of McGrath who was released on Sunday.
